renderPacket.identity: Real Borobudur Temple in Central Java from terrace level on the upper circular terraces: multiple unmistakable perforated bell-shaped stone stupas across foreground and midground, the monumental central stupa anchoring the temple identity, broad horizontal 3:2 one-continuous-camera-view composition, distant Kedu Valley and volcanic silhouette only softly visible through natural morning haze while the stone stupas remain dominant, soft early-morning light with restrained warm-grey volcanic stone, muted green valley and pale sky, photo 6 to quiet watercolor 4, refined painterly realism; preserve real Borobudur proportions and stone texture; no saturated tourism-poster sunrise, giant Buddha, fantasy temple extensions, prayer flags, ceremonial crowd, readable signage, labels or text.

Real Bromo Tengger Semeru landscape from the Penanjakan area in East Java: Mount Bromo's smoking crater cone and Mount Batok clearly separated in foreground/midground, Semeru rising farther behind when visibility allows, broad Tengger sand sea and layered volcanic relief explaining the caldera scale, cool early-morning or soft daylight with restrained natural mist that does not hide the landforms; no fantasy eruption, lava, oversized plume, dense tourist silhouettes or saturated poster sunrise.

Real Jatiluwih terraced rice landscape in Bali: layered green paddies following the hillside with visible subak irrigation geometry, palms and tropical vegetation at natural scale, broad oblique hillside composition rather than a vertical drone pattern, soft humid daylight and natural greens; no staged farmer portrait, tourist swing, resort deck, decorative gate or neon saturation.

Real Padar Island high viewpoint in Komodo National Park: recognisable sequence of dry savanna ridges and several crescent-shaped bays opening to blue-green sea, one continuous natural high-landscape view at plausible human viewpoint height, dry-season ochre and olive ridges under clear or lightly hazy daylight; no giant Komodo dragon, exaggerated pink beach, enlarged boats, impossible drone altitude or tourism-poster saturation.

Real Piaynemo elevated viewpoint in Raja Ampat, Southwest Papua: clusters of steep densely forested limestone islets separated by clear turquoise-to-deep-blue channels, broad oblique humid tropical seascape with natural depth and plausible water colour; no vertical map-like view, overwater villas, fantasy rock spires, giant boats, invented beaches or hyper-saturated lagoon colour.

Real Ke'te Kesu' village in the Toraja highlands of South Sulawesi: coherent row of traditional tongkonan houses and rice barns with strongly curved roofs, set within real rice-field and highland surroundings, architecture clearly readable at scene-card scale while landscape context remains visible, restrained timber, red, black and green tones under soft daylight; no funeral staging, exposed remains, ceremonial crowd, fantasy roof exaggeration, souvenir-shop emphasis or readable signage.

Real Lake Toba and Samosir caldera landscape from an elevated western-Samosir or Holbung-area viewpoint in North Sumatra: vast blue lake enclosed by long caldera walls and rolling highland ridges, Samosir terrain clearly occupying part of the composition, natural grass slope as a scale anchor, soft clear daylight and atmospheric depth; no staged selfie point, decorative swing, alpine snow, fantasy fjord cliffs, giant boats or impossible island geometry.

Real Bundaran HI in central Jakarta: the Welcome Monument and fountain as the spatial anchor with contemporary towers forming the surrounding city canyon, broad street-level or slightly elevated urban composition that reads as a lived metropolis rather than a monument close-up, early morning or restrained blue-hour light with normal city movement visible; no cyberpunk treatment, invented towers, giant flags, empty ceremonial plaza, legible billboards or generated signage.

Real Sekonyer River corridor in Tanjung Puting National Park, Central Kalimantan: tea-brown tropical river winding between dense lowland and peat-swamp rainforest walls, humid soft daylight with layered greens and brown water, at most one small traditional river boat as a secondary scale cue; no inserted orangutan portrait, fantasy jungle, staged feeding platform, resort structure or dramatic storm.
